title: No table and no column are named for the occupancy refusal, the eviction status or the eviction record
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2.md (T3.1, T3.2); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3.md (A2.8.3.1, A2.8.3.2); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-021 Data); _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5)
section: Metadata (Patterns applied); s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 and 6; s8 BR1, BR5; s9; s11 Data; s13 Database and migrations
description: The eviction step must hold the occupancy state of the held asset, the eviction status and the reference of the instruction raised to Legal. TSD S5 T3.1 defines only asset (DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042), listing and asset_sale, and none of them carries an occupancy or an eviction field; TSD S5 T3.2 gives no list for either; the FSD A2.8 field catalog repeats the v_ace_npa_asset and v_ace_collateral fields only; the legacy Data table lists recovery_case, assignment, v_ace_npa_asset, partner_instruction, decision_log_entry and rule_row and no eviction entity. The story therefore writes the three values against the asset row where a column exists and records the rest as Not specified in the source documents rather than inventing a table, a column or a list.
evidence: TSD S5 v2 T3.1 asset DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 with holding_status and holding_cost_to_date and no occupancy or eviction field; T3.2 LOV-ASSET-TYPE, LOV-HOLDING, LOV-LISTING, LOV-SALE-CHANNEL, LOV-SEGMENT and LOV-TRANSFER-IN only; FSD S5 v3 A2.8.3.2 field catalog of v_ace_npa_asset and v_ace_collateral columns; legacy RWB-E4-021 Data table with no eviction entity; _work/msr/context/S5.md table rows asset_sale and listing.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the data steward
proposed: The S5 data owner names the columns of the occupancy state, the eviction status and the instruction reference on the asset table, or names the store that holds the eviction record, and the DB story of the service adds them in its own Flyway sequence; until then the values are held against the asset row and read as configuration.

title: No source publishes an operation for the officer action, the stage signal or the case-move answer, and none names how the eviction instruction reaches Legal
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (REST operations provided, connection matrix row S5 Asset); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2.md (appendix T-A.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-021 Endpoints); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-DIS-13)
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1 and 7; s7 AC1, AC2; s8 BR3, BR4, BR7; s12.1, s12.2, s12.4, s12.8; s13
description: The feature needs four surfaces that no source publishes: the officer action that records the occupancy refusal, the stage signal the parent forwards to the running child, the case-move answer that carries EVICTION_REQUIRED and the instruction to Legal, and the route by which that instruction reaches rwb-litigation. The ownership rows of S5 carry six operations and none of them is an eviction operation; TSD S5 T-A.1 lists API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 only; the legacy Endpoints table names two GET reads; and the connection matrix gives S5 no REST or Temporal line to S4 and only an event line from S4, while Architecture v5 slide 13 sends every fact of another service through the case router and the parent. The story therefore builds the surface as the stage signal and the case-move answer, with their names stubbed, and raises the instruction on the answer instead of calling Legal.
evidence: _work/msr/context/S5.md REST operations provided: GET /assets, GET /assets/{assetId}, GET /assets/{assetKey}, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings, POST /assets/{assetKey}/listings, POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds; TSD S5 v2 T-A.1 rows API-S5-001 to API-S5-005; legacy RWB-E4-021 Endpoints rows GET /api/recovery/v1/assets/{assetId} and GET /api/recovery/v1/assets; context pack slide 13 matrix row S5 Asset with P7 T, S4 E, P8 T E, S9 T E and no S4 call; Architecture v5 slide 13 note that events reach the case through the case router and the parent forwards them to the child.
owner_role: P3 rwb-case owner with the S5 rwb-asset owner and the S4 rwb-litigation owner
proposed: rwb-case publishes the name of the signal it forwards and of the stage answer it accepts, and confirms that it routes the instruction to rwb-litigation; the S5 contract replaces the placeholder with the published name in a minor version and the application story changes only its adapter.

title: The split plan carries no requirement row for the application slice, and the requirement is taken from TSD S5 T8
source: _work/msr/plan (slice RWB-S5-E4021-APP reqs); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2.md (T8); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3.md (A1.2, A2.8)
section: s2 Business rationale; s18 Traceability requirement table
description: The story serves FEAT-AST-08 of the FSD module S5 and the slice carries an empty requirement list. TSD S5 T8 maps REQ-S5-006 to REQ-S5-010 to FEAT-AST-08, so the traceability table cites those five module requirements and names the missing plan row instead of leaving the table empty or inventing an identifier.
evidence: Slice RWB-S5-E4021-APP with reqs as an empty list; TSD S5 v2 T8 rows REQ-S5-006 to REQ-S5-010 each mapped to FEAT-AST-08; FSD S5 v3 A1.2 row FEAT-AST-08 and A2.8.
owner_role: Program requirements owner with the business analyst
proposed: The requirement owner allocates a plan row for the slice at the next plan revision and the traceability row is repointed without a story change.

title: The legacy screen list gives SCR-22 four states and names no eviction state, and no source names the state the screen shows
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-021 Screen and states); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-DIS-13, R-DIS-14); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2.md (T3.2)
section: s15 Screens and states; s4 Flow step 11; s5 X3
description: SCR-22 Asset record is listed with the states Take-on, held, listed and sold, and SCR-21 Asset list with Loading and list. The case route carries EVICTION_REQUIRED and the rule raises an eviction against a held asset, so the screen presents a state the legacy list does not name, and LOV-HOLDING offers HELD, LISTED, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD, TRANSFERRED and RENTED with no eviction value. The story shows the eviction state of the asset on SCR-22 and records that its name and presentation are not specified in the sources.
evidence: legacy RWB-E4-021 Screen and states table: SCR-21 Asset list Loading and list, SCR-22 Asset record Take-on, held, listed and sold; Business Rules v4 R-DIS-13 to EVICTION_REQUIRED and R-DIS-14 to ASSET_HELD; TSD S5 v2 T3.2 LOV-HOLDING with six values and no eviction value.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the screen designer of the gateway-bff composite route
proposed: The screen designer names the eviction state of SCR-22 in the composite route specification of RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the reference-data owner confirms whether LOV-HOLDING gains a value or the eviction state stays an element of the asset answer.

title: The contract baseline declares no eviction operation and no named column for the eviction element, because no source gives either
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (ownership rows of S5); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2.md (T3.1, appendix T-A.1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2.md (T3.0)
section: Metadata (Patterns applied); s3 Preconditions; s7 C2, C4; s9; s11 Data; s12.1, s12.7, s12.8; s15
description: The baseline must declare the surface of the eviction step and the elements of the eviction state, and no source gives either. The six ownership rows of S5 name no eviction operation, TSD S5 T-A.1 lists five operations of which none is an eviction, and TSD S5 T3.1 gives the asset object no occupancy, eviction or instruction column. The baseline therefore declares the step's own operation as None with this gap, declares the eviction element with its type and its source and no column, and names the asset table as S5's although the ownership table list carries asset_sale and listing only.
evidence: _work/msr/context/S5.md REST operations provided (six rows, none an eviction) and table rows asset_sale and listing; TSD S5 v2 appendix T-A.1 API-S5-001 to API-S5-005; TSD S5 v2 T3.1 asset DF-COL-028 to DF-COL-042 and T3.0 standard columns.
owner_role: S5 rwb-asset service owner with the solution architect
proposed: The service owner confirms at the tag whether the step exposes an operation and where the eviction element lives; the baseline adds the operation and the column in a minor version, and the ownership map adds the asset row in its next revision.

title: The stage signal, the case-move answer and the eviction instruction have no published element names, and no call type is given from rwb-asset to rwb-litigation
source: _work/msr/context/S5.md (connection matrix row S5 Asset); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (as summarised in the context pack: slide 13); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-DIS-13, R-DIS-14)
description: The baseline must declare the elements of the occupancy fact, the possession result and the case-move answer, and the call type of the instruction to Legal. Architecture v5 slide 13 fixes the boundary and names no element; the connection matrix gives S5 a Temporal line to P7 and event lines from S4, and no line of any type from S5 to S4, so the instruction cannot be declared as a call of this service; no source names an eviction or possession event of rwb-litigation. The baseline declares the signal and the answer with the placeholder for their element names, declares no event and no subscription, and states that the instruction travels on the case answer.
evidence: _work/msr/context/S5.md connection matrix row S5 Asset with columns P3 blank, P7 T, S4 E, P8 T E, S9 T E; Architecture v5 slide 13 notes on the case router and the parent forwarding facts to the running child; Business Rules v4 R-DIS-13 systems LIT, Partner Portal with owner Litigation officer; R-DIS-14 systems Workbench, LIT.
owner_role: Solution architect with the owners of rwb-case and rwb-litigation
proposed: rwb-case publishes the element names of the signal and the answer and confirms it routes the instruction to rwb-litigation; if S4 later publishes an eviction event, the baseline declares it as consumed in a minor version.
